title: Phase-aware sequence thermostat and sparse-signal denoiser for drift-resilient profiling
author: Marisol Ortega
release_notes: Add phase-aware workload runner and signal-denoising pipeline to improve stability of kernel-level profiling under thermal/jittered conditions.
description: Motivation: existing workload runners exercise steady-state and bursty traffic but do not mimic slow, thermal-like drift and micro-jitter observed on GPU fleets during long runs. This causes noise in p95/p99 profiling baselines and makes regression detection brittle. This PR introduces a phase-aware sequence thermostat workload and a sparse-signal denoiser + windowed hotspot reconciler so profiling baselines are resilient to thermal drift and measurement noise. Changes include: 1) bench/runners/phase_thermostat.py: a new workload runner that emits sequences with controlled inter-request drift, frequency-domain jitter, and epochal thermal profiles (configurable ramp, hold, cool). 2) bench/telemetry/denoiser.py: a lightweight filtering stage that removes high-frequency sampling noise and reconstructs per-kernel time series using median-window and spectral thresholding heuristics. 3) bench/reporters/window_reconciler.py: merges overlapping hotspot windows across epochs to produce stable per-kernel baselines and highlights persistent regressions. 4) perf/artifacts/phase_baselines/: new baseline outputs (flamegraphs, kernel-sample histograms, PSD plots) with metadata. 5) tests/integration/test_phase_thermostat.py and tests/unit/test_denoiser.py: coverage for runner and denoiser edges. 6) CI: add perf-sim job that runs a short synthetic epoch on PRs to validate non-regression of the denoiser. Commits and files changed listed below. Rationale: by simulating slow drift + micro-jitter we can detect regressions that only manifest under thermal conditions (e.g., scheduler backpressure, small kernel regressions amplified under slow-down). The denoiser reconciles noisy samples so alerts are driven by meaningful signals, lowering false positives in the benchmark pipeline. Backwards compatibility: runner and denoiser are opt-in via benchmark configs; default global pipelines unchanged. Rollout: merge to main, land behind a feature flag, enable perf-sim CI for benchmark-lab. Linked linear tickets: ENG-1423 (phase-aware runner), ENG-1560 (denoiser & reconciler), SUP-418 (customer-reported noise during nightly profiling).
